The bouncer is admiring an antiporter. An antiporter is a type of transmembrane protein that allows the movement of two different molecules or ions in opposite directions.  The bouncer lets one person in for every two people that leave the club.  This means that for every 2 people moving in one direction, 1 person is moving in the opposite direction.  This is an example of antiport.  A uniporter is a type of transmembrane protein that allows the movement of a single molecule or ion across the membrane.  A symporter is a type of transmembrane protein that allows the movement of two different molecules or ions in the same direction.  A GPCR is a type of transmembrane protein that allows the movement of signals across the membrane.

Virchow's triad is a set of three factors that are thought to contribute to the formation of a thrombus (blood clot) in the body. The three factors are:Alteration in the integrity of the vessel wall - this can occur due to trauma, atherosclerosis or other forms of damage. This exposes collagen and other sub-endothelial components of the vessel wall to the blood. This can lead to platelet adhesion and activation. Alteration in the composition of the blood to render it hyper-coagulative - this can occur due to the presence of clotting factors or other pro-coagulant substances in the blood. This can lead to the formation of a fibrin mesh. Alteration in blood flow - this can occur due to venous stasis, turbulence or hyper-flow. Stasis of blood can lead to the formation of a clot.  The principles of Virchow's triad can be applied to many disease processes, including myocardial infarction (MI) caused by a ruptured atherosclerotic plaque.

The correct answer is C. Paracetamol is normally metabolized in the liver via UGT enzymes, but in a toxic dose, the UGT enzymes become saturated. This means that paracetamol is then metabolized by cytochrome P450 enzymes, which produce a toxic metabolite called NAPBQI. This NAPBQI is normally deactivated by hepatic glutathione, but in a toxic dose, the glutathione stores are depleted. This means that NAPBQI accumulates in the liver and causes hepatocyte necrosis.  N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is a drug that can be used to treat paracetamol overdose. It works by replenishing hepatic glutathione stores, and so deactivating NAPBQI.  A) Cytochrome P450 enzymes - incorrect. These enzymes are responsible for metabolizing paracetamol into NAPBQI in a toxic dose.B) Hepatic glutathione - incorrect. This is the substance that normally deactivates NAPBQI, but in a toxic dose, the stores of glutathione are depleted.D) n-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPBQI) - incorrect. This is the toxic metabolite of paracetamol that causes hepatocyte necrosis.E) UGT enzymes - incorrect. These enzymes are responsible for the normal metabolism of paracetamol.

Vitamin A is also known as retinol and is found in carrots, leafy greens and liver. It is also known as vitamin eye, as it is essential for the formation of Rhodopsin. Rhodopsin is a light-sensitive pigment found in the night-rod cells of the retina. Rhodopsin is a receptor that allows the eye to adapt to low light levels. Vitamin A is fat soluble, and so, it is possible that the excessive vitamin E in this patient's system has inhibited the absorption of vitamin A.

The glenoid labrum is a fibrocartilaginous ring that surrounds the glenoid fossa of the scapula. It is formed from the glenoid deep to the joint capsule and is a rim of fibrocartilage that deepens the shallow glenoid fossa, increasing the stability of the glenohumeral joint.
